overall: AG found no Open Meeting Law violation. The chair may decide who speaks at a meeting, so not recognizing an abutter during public comment was lawful. The misinformation claim was not an OML issue.

allegations.summary: Complainant, an abutter, alleged he was not allowed to speak in opposition to a roof deck variance at an April 6 remote hearing.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, because it is within the chair’s discretion to limit public participation during a meeting, the chair did not violate the Open Meeting Law by preventing Mr. Harter from addressing the Board during the April 6 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board was misinformed about the variance and its impact on abutters, and that his comments might have changed the outcome.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.
